metadata.methodology: Extracted only from directly retrieved clinical sources during this session. No LLM inference used for intervention recommendations. Common aliases field uses general knowledge for alternate phrasings only. All intervention entries include source attribution. The 2026-06-17 update added the MindScope behavioral/emotional condition set (anxiety_school_avoidance, emotional_dysregulation, depression_withdrawal, trauma_response, oppositional_defiant_behavior, social_isolation, self_harm_risk) for a school-based behavioral health care plan system. New conditions were sourced only from SAMHSA, NIMH, AACAP, CDC, AAP, and university medical centers (University of North Texas Center for Play Therapy, Yale Medicine, University of Washington). Conditions reflect behavioral presentations observed by guidance counselors rather than formal DSM diagnoses; where a presentation (e.g., social_isolation, emotional_dysregulation, self_harm_risk) is not itself a diagnosis, recommendations were mapped from the closest evidence-based clinical literature and caveats are recorded in source_notes and gaps_and_limitations. New-condition entries use the category set therapy, evaluation, school_support, medication_management, community_support. The therapy_to_query_map sibling key was added to translate intervention names into external-API search terminology. This knowledge base is not a crisis-response tool; self_harm_risk entries point to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

recommended.rationale: Behavioral approaches have the most evidence for treating symptoms of ASD and are widely accepted among educators and healthcare professionals. Early intensive behavioral intervention improves outcomes for many children with autism.

sources.what_it_said: Behavioral approaches have the most evidence for treating symptoms of ASD. ABA encourages desired behaviors and discourages undesired behaviors.
Evidence supports the use of behavioral interventions (e.g., applied behavior analysis) for skill building.
ABA is considered an evidence-based best practice treatment by the US Surgeon General and by the American Psychological Association.

recommended.source_notes: CDC, AAP, and Autism Speaks all endorse ABA for children with ASD. Programs providing 25-40 hours/week for 1-3 years show gains per Autism Speaks. The ESDM variant is specifically for ages 12-48 months.

recommended.rationale: ESDM is a broad developmental approach based on ABA principles used with children 12-48 months. Parents and therapists use play and social exchanges to improve language, social, and learning skills.

sources.what_it_said: ESDM is used with children 12-48 months of age. Parents and therapists use play, social exchanges in natural settings to improve language and social skills.

recommended.source_notes: Age-specific to 12-48 months. Falls at the younger end of this age bracket.

recommended.rationale: Speech and language therapy is the most common developmental therapy for people with ASD, helping improve understanding and use of speech and language. Most children with ASD participate in it.

sources.what_it_said: The most common developmental therapy for people with ASD is speech and language therapy, which improves understanding and use of speech and language.
Most children with ASD participate in speech-language therapy. SLT addresses a range of challenges often faced by people with autism.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. Placed here as applicable across all ages.

recommended.rationale: Occupational therapy teaches skills that help the person live as independently as possible, including dressing, eating, bathing, and relating to people. It can include sensory integration therapy.

sources.what_it_said: Occupational therapy teaches skills for independent living including dressing, eating, bathing, and can include sensory integration therapy.
Occupational therapy addresses a combination of cognitive, physical and motor skills to increase independence and participation.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. CDC also notes OT may include sensory integration therapy and physical therapy components.

recommended.rationale: Early intervention services help children from birth to 3 years learn important skills. Research shows early intervention can greatly improve a child's development.

sources.what_it_said: Early intervention services help children from birth to 3 years learn important skills. Research shows early intervention can greatly improve development.
Pediatricians should refer children to early intervention (0-3 years) or school services to initiate services.

recommended.source_notes: Primarily for ages 0-3, but transition to school-based services occurs at age 3. Still relevant as transition planning for 3-5 age group.

recommended.rationale: Children with disabilities, including ASD, may be eligible for services through the local education system beginning at age 3. Eligible children can begin to receive services prior to formally starting school.

sources.what_it_said: Children with ASD may be eligible for services through local education beginning at age 3. They often have an IEP or 504 plan.

recommended.source_notes: Applies from age 3 onward under IDEA Part B.

recommended.rationale: DIR encourages parents and therapists to follow the interests of the individual to expand opportunities for communication.

sources.what_it_said: The Developmental, Individual Differences, Relationship-Based model (DIR or Floortime) follows the child's interests to expand communication opportunities.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. Listed as a social-relational approach by CDC.

recommended.rationale: Behavioral therapists providing ABA and other interventions play a critical role in a child's treatment. Parents should select interventionists who view the family as teammates.

sources.what_it_said: Families who are required to implement drill-type interventions have greater stress. Interventions incorporated into daily routines are preferred.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. Autism Speaks emphasizes families as teammates in intervention.

recommended.rationale: ABA encourages desired behaviors and discourages undesired behaviors to improve a variety of skills. Progress is tracked and measured.

sources.what_it_said: ABA encourages desired behaviors and discourages undesired behaviors to improve a variety of skills. Progress is tracked and measured.
More than 20 studies show intensive ABA therapy (25-40 hours/week) improves intellectual functioning, language, daily living, and social functioning.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. ABA continues to be evidence-based across childhood.

recommended.rationale: Most children with ASD participate in speech-language therapy. SLT coordinates the mechanics of speech with the meaning and social use of language.

sources.what_it_said: Most children with ASD participate in speech-language therapy. SLT coordinates speech mechanics with meaning and social use of language.
Speech and language therapy helps improve understanding and use of speech and language.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific.

recommended.rationale: OT helps the person increase independence and participate more fully in life. It often includes sensory integration therapy to improve responses to sensory input.

sources.what_it_said: OT can include sensory integration therapy to improve responses to sensory input that may be restrictive or overwhelming.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific.

sources.what_it_said: TEACCH is based on consistency and visual learning. It adjusts classroom structure and improves academic and other outcomes.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. Classified as an educational approach by CDC. Most applicable in school-age settings.

sources.what_it_said: Social skills groups provide opportunities for people with ASD to practice social skills in a structured environment.
Social skills training in one-on-one and peer group settings is a common treatment for individuals with autism.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. Autism Speaks notes it is not an official certified therapy but commonly provided.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. CDC references a trial specifically for children with high-functioning ASD and anxiety.

sources.what_it_said: For children under 6, AAP recommends parent training in behavior management as the first line of treatment, before medication.

sources.what_it_said: Behavior therapy works as well as medication in young children with ADHD. Improvements persist for several years after treatment.

sources.what_it_said: Methylphenidate may be used in children 4-6 years if behavioral interventions do not provide significant improvement.

recommended.source_notes: ASHA-referenced guideline recommends parent-based intervention as initial approach for expressive delay.

recommended.rationale: Early identification and intervention can mitigate the impact of risk factors. Children who show signs of a problem should be referred to an early intervention program.

sources.what_it_said: Early identification and intervention can mitigate the impact of risk factors.
If your child shows signs of a problem, the SLP may suggest an early intervention program to help communicate better.

recommended.source_notes: Part C early intervention applies to children under 3. School-based services begin at age 3.

recommended.rationale: A combination of parent-based and child-centered interventions should be considered for children with receptive language deficits or risk factors for developmental language disorder.

sources.what_it_said: A combination of parent-based and child-centered interventions should be considered for receptive language deficits or DLD risk factors.

recommended.source_notes: Particularly recommended when receptive language is affected, not just expressive.

recommended.rationale: The overall goal of intervention is to stimulate language development and teach skills to enhance communication and access academic content.

sources.what_it_said: Areas targeted include improving intelligibility, increasing vocabulary, semantic relationships, and morpheme acquisition.
The overall goal of intervention is to stimulate language development and teach skills to enhance communication and academic content access.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — applicable across school age. ASHA notes intervention is child-specific based on current functioning level.

recommended.rationale: Children with language disorders may be eligible for school-based services. SLPs are involved in the RTI process and can provide instruction to struggling students.

sources.what_it_said: SLPs can have several roles in the RTI process to identify children with disabilities and provide instruction to struggling students.
SLPs may work on a team to test your child. The team includes the parent, child's teacher, and others.

recommended.source_notes: ASHA emphasizes that educators cannot use RTI to delay or deny an evaluation for special education eligibility.

recommended.rationale: Children with DLD should receive treatments targeting their area of need, including vocabulary intervention for lexical-semantic impairments.

sources.what_it_said: Lexical-semantic impairments should receive vocabulary intervention including word understanding, production, and expression.
Target areas include academic vocabulary and improving semantic depth or richness of familiar words.

recommended.source_notes: ASHA practice portal specifically identifies vocabulary and syntax as key intervention targets for school-age children.

recommended.rationale: If appropriate, an assessment of augmentative or alternative communication may be conducted for children who need support beyond verbal speech.

sources.what_it_said: If appropriate, an assessment of an alternative or augmentative form of communication may be conducted.

recommended.source_notes: Applicable when verbal communication is insufficient. ASHA references their AAC Practice Portal page.

recommended.rationale: Language problems in older children may show up in different ways. The impact of developmental language disorder persists into adulthood, requiring continued intervention.

sources.what_it_said: Language problems in older children may show up as difficulties with reading, writing, and following complex directions.
The impact of DLD persists into adulthood. Symptoms include limited complex sentences, difficulty finding words, and reading problems.

recommended.source_notes: NIDCD notes that DLD symptoms in older children/adults include reading problems, disorganized writing, and grammatical errors.

recommended.rationale: Adolescents with spoken language disorders may continue to need school-based support for academic success, particularly for reading and writing.

sources.what_it_said: SLPs play a role in the RTI process and provide instruction to struggling students across age groups.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. ASHA notes language disorders can affect reading and writing.

recommended.intervention: Occupational Therapy Using Sensory Integration Approach
recommended.rationale: Occupational therapy using Ayres Sensory Integration is an evidence-based manualized intervention in which practitioners use individually tailored, purposeful, playful, sensory-rich activities to promote adaptive behaviors.

sources.what_it_said: ASI is an evidence-based manualized intervention using individually tailored, playful, sensory-rich activities to promote adaptive behaviors.
Children are most commonly treated for SPD with occupational therapy (OT) that may be supplemented with listening therapy.

recommended.source_notes: AOTA describes ASI as evidence-based for autistic children with emerging evidence for children with idiopathic sensory integration differences. General recommendation — not age-specific.

recommended.rationale: Early diagnosis increases the chances of successful intervention and can prevent secondary problems from developing such as behavior problems and poor self-esteem.

sources.what_it_said: Early diagnosis increases chances of successful intervention and can prevent secondary problems like behavior issues and poor self-esteem.
Assessment data indicated occupational performance affected by difficulty processing sensory information, motor skill limitations, and self-regulation challenges.

recommended.source_notes: STAR Institute uses standardized assessments (SIPT, MAP, M-Fun) along with observation and parent/caregiver interviews.

recommended.rationale: AOTA systematic reviews include parent and teacher education/coaching as a key intervention category. STAR Institute builds parent education into every individualized treatment program.

sources.what_it_said: Practice guidelines include: Interventions That Provide Education or Coaching of Parents or Teachers.
STAR Institute builds a significant parent education component into every individualized treatment program.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. Both AOTA and STAR Institute emphasize family-centered approach.

recommended.rationale: AOTA systematic reviews address specific sensory techniques and sensory environmental modifications as an evidence-based intervention category.

sources.what_it_said: Practice guidelines include: Interventions That Address Specific Sensory Techniques and Sensory Environmental Modifications.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific. AOTA includes this as a distinct intervention category in their practice guidelines.

recommended.intervention: Occupational Therapy Using Sensory Integration Approach (School-Based)
recommended.rationale: 65% of school-based OT practitioners report sensory-related issues are frequently or always the reason for OT referrals. Challenges with sensory processing affect children's ability to successfully engage in school occupations.

sources.what_it_said: 65% of school-based OT practitioners report sensory issues are frequently/always the reason for referrals.

recommended.source_notes: AOTA's 2025 article specifically calls for increased use of ASI principles in school settings using multitiered supports.

recommended.rationale: AOTA systematic reviews include cognitive and occupation-based interventions as a distinct evidence-based category for children with sensory integration challenges.

sources.what_it_said: Practice guidelines include: Cognitive and Occupation-Based Interventions as a category of intervention.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific.

recommended.intervention: Sensory Environmental Modifications and Accommodations (School Setting)
recommended.rationale: Interventions using principles of ASI can be applied across all tiers of a multitiered system of supports in schools.

sources.what_it_said: ASI principles can be used across all tiers of a multitiered system of supports in schools.

recommended.source_notes: AOTA provides examples for implementing sensory supports within existing school structures.

recommended.rationale: Education or coaching of parents or teachers is identified as a key intervention approach in AOTA practice guidelines for sensory challenges.

sources.what_it_said: Practice guidelines include: Interventions That Provide Education or Coaching of Parents or Teachers.

recommended.source_notes: General recommendation — not age-specific.

recommended.intervention: Occupational Therapy with Sensory Integration Approach (Adolescent)
recommended.rationale: Adolescents who received therapy in childhood may find themselves struggling at new developmental levels. Short bursts of therapy or counseling that increases self-understanding is often extremely helpful.

sources.what_it_said: Adolescents who benefited from childhood therapy may struggle at new developmental levels. Short bursts of therapy are often extremely helpful.
Effective services for adults and older adolescents include direct therapy, home programs, education, and/or accommodations.

recommended.source_notes: STAR Institute specifically addresses adolescent and adult needs as distinct from younger children.

recommended.rationale: Education about sensory processing helps the individual develop personal insight and accommodations to modify the negative impact of SPD on daily life.

sources.what_it_said: Education about sensory processing contributes to personal insight so the individual can develop accommodations to sensory-based differences.

recommended.source_notes: Primarily from STAR Institute's adolescent/adult program. Important for transitioning to self-management.

recommended.rationale: Home programs and accommodations can be utilized to reduce negative symptoms associated with sensory processing differences.

sources.what_it_said: Home programs can be utilized, with some limited direct treatment, to reduce negative symptoms of sensory integration differences.

recommended.source_notes: STAR Institute notes many adolescents/adults do well with evaluation and consultation for treatment rather than intensive direct therapy.

recommended.rationale: Persistent or extreme fear and avoidance could be due to an anxiety disorder, and an evaluation helps determine the best diagnosis and treatment. Some signs of anxiety could also be caused by other conditions, such as trauma.

sources.what_it_said: The first step to treatment is to talk with a health care provider, such as the child's primary care provider or a mental health specialist, about getting an evaluation. It is important to get a careful evaluation to get the best diagnosis and treatment.

recommended.source_notes: CDC frames evaluation as the first step for any concern about anxiety in children.

recommended.rationale: Behavior therapy for anxiety helps children cope with and manage anxiety symptoms while gradually exposing them to their fears. For very young children, involving parents in treatment is key.

sources.what_it_said: Behavior therapy for anxiety may involve helping children cope with and manage anxiety symptoms while gradually exposing them to their fears. For very young children, involving parents in treatment is key.

recommended.source_notes: CDC emphasizes parent involvement for the youngest children. Formal CBT is generally introduced in older children.

recommended.rationale: Play therapy uses toys, drawings, and games to help young children recognize, identify, and verbalize feelings they cannot yet express in words, including fear and anxiety.

sources.what_it_said: Play Therapy involves the use of toys, blocks, dolls, puppets, drawings, and games to help the child recognize, identify, and verbalize feelings. Through a combination of talk and play the child has an opportunity to better understand and manage their conflicts, feelings, and behavior.

sources.organization: University of North Texas Center for Play Therapy
sources.what_it_said: Child-Centered Play Therapy is a developmentally responsive, play-based intervention for young children ages 3 to 10 and is designated as a promising evidence-based mental health intervention by the Title IV-E Prevention Services Clearinghouse and the California Evidence-Based Clearinghouse for Child Welfare.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP describes play therapy as a recognized psychotherapy type. The UNT Center for Play Therapy is the university body that developed the evidence-based CCPT protocol for ages 3-10.

recommended.intervention: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) with Graduated Exposure
recommended.rationale: CBT is the current gold standard for treating anxiety disorders in children, working by changing dysfunctional thoughts and using gradual exposure to anxiety-provoking situations such as returning to school. AACAP recommends CBT for patients 6 to 18 years old with separation, social, or generalized anxiety.

sources.what_it_said: CBT, which involves changing dysfunctional thoughts and behaviors through gradual exposure to anxiety-provoking stimuli, is the current gold standard for treating anxiety disorders in children.

AACAP recommends that cognitive-behavioral therapy be offered to patients 6 to 18 years old with social anxiety, generalized anxiety, separation anxiety, specific phobia, or panic disorder. Both CBT and SSRI medication have considerable empirical support as safe and effective short-term treatments for anxiety in children and adolescents.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP full Clinical Practice Guideline text on jaacap.org is subscription-based; recommendation statements were accessible via the article.

recommended.intervention: School-Based Support and Graduated Re-Entry Plan (504/IEP)
recommended.rationale: Treatment of school refusal requires the family, child, school, and therapist to work together on a plan to gradually return the child to school in small, supported steps. Specific plans for anxiety management at school can be written into a 504 plan or IEP.

sources.what_it_said: Treatment often requires family, child, school, and therapist to work together. Children develop a plan to gradually practice returning to school in small, supported steps, which may include shortened school days, check-ins with a trusted adult, and accommodations through a 504 plan or Individualized Education Plan.

School-directed interventions that educate teachers about the student's anxiety can be part of the treatment plan; specific plans for anxiety management at school can be written into the student's 504 plan or IEP, such as graduated school re-entry with contingent rewards for separation anxiety.

recommended.source_notes: Strong consensus across AACAP family materials and clinical guideline that school collaboration and graduated re-entry are central to school avoidance.

recommended.rationale: Family-directed interventions that improve parent-child relationships, strengthen problem-solving and communication, reduce parental anxiety, and foster anxiety-reducing parenting skills often supplement individual treatment for childhood anxiety.

sources.what_it_said: Family-directed interventions that improve parent-child relationships, strengthen family problem-solving and communication skills, reduce parental anxiety, and foster anxiety-reducing parenting skills often supplement individual treatment.

recommended.source_notes: Described by AACAP as a supplement to individual CBT rather than a stand-alone treatment.

recommended.rationale: For adolescents, CBT has considerable empirical support as a safe and effective short-term treatment for anxiety. In the NIMH-funded CAMS trial, CBT alone helped 60 percent of youth, and combining CBT with an SSRI helped 81 percent.

sources.what_it_said: Both cognitive-behavioral therapy and SSRI medication have considerable empirical support as safe and effective short-term treatments for anxiety in children and adolescents.

In the Child/Adolescent Anxiety Multimodal Study (CAMS), 81 percent improved on combination treatment, 60 percent in the CBT-only group, and 55 percent in the sertraline-only group, supporting CBT, SSRI, or their combination as effective options.

recommended.source_notes: CAMS enrolled children ages 7-17, supporting CBT across this adolescent group.

recommended.intervention: Medication Management (SSRI) for Moderate to Severe Anxiety
recommended.rationale: SSRI medication has considerable empirical support for anxiety in adolescents and, when combined with CBT, produces the highest response rates. Medication decisions should be made with a health care provider.

sources.what_it_said: Combination treatment with the SSRI sertraline plus CBT was the most effective option in the CAMS trial, and sertraline alone showed a good response rate as well.
SSRI medication has considerable empirical support as a safe and effective short-term treatment for anxiety in children and adolescents.

recommended.source_notes: Medication is recommended in combination with therapy, not as a stand-alone treatment for school avoidance per AACAP family materials.

recommended.rationale: School refusal in the older child or adolescent is generally a more serious problem and often requires more intensive treatment, with the school supporting a structured and timely return through a 504 plan or IEP.

sources.what_it_said: The school should support the family and treatment provider's plan for successful school attendance through the development of a 504 plan or Individualized Education Plan. Refusal to go to school in the older child or adolescent is generally a more serious illness and often requires more intensive treatment.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP notes adolescent school refusal is generally more serious than in younger children.

recommended.rationale: For younger children with disruptive, dysregulated behavior, the treatment with the strongest evidence is behavior therapy training for parents, in which a therapist helps the parent strengthen the parent-child relationship and respond effectively to the child's behavior.

sources.what_it_said: For younger children, the treatment with the strongest evidence is behavior therapy training for parents, where a therapist helps the parent learn effective ways to strengthen the parent-child relationship and respond to the child's behavior.

recommended.source_notes: CDC frames parent-focused behavior therapy as the strongest-evidence approach for behavioral and emotional regulation problems in young children.

recommended.rationale: Play therapy helps young children recognize, identify, and verbalize feelings and better understand and manage their conflicts, feelings, and behavior through play.

sources.what_it_said: Play Therapy uses toys, blocks, dolls, puppets, drawings, and games to help the child recognize, identify, and verbalize feelings, giving the child an opportunity to better understand and manage their conflicts, feelings, and behavior.

sources.organization: University of North Texas Center for Play Therapy
sources.what_it_said: Child outcomes following Child-Centered Play Therapy include decreased symptomatic behaviors and improvement in overall functioning.

recommended.source_notes: Play therapy targets emotional expression and self-regulation in early childhood.

recommended.rationale: Severe, frequent emotional outbursts and chronic irritability can overlap with several conditions, so a comprehensive evaluation by a trained mental health professional is important to identify the underlying cause and plan treatment.

sources.what_it_said: Some symptoms associated with severe irritability and outbursts are also present in other child psychiatric disorders, which is why it is particularly important to get a comprehensive evaluation by a trained and qualified mental health professional.

recommended.source_notes: Drawn from AACAP guidance on disruptive mood dysregulation disorder, the clinical analogue for chronic irritability and emotional dysregulation.

recommended.rationale: For chronic irritability and emotional dysregulation, treatment generally includes psychotherapy first, with medication added later if needed. CBT helps children change negative thought patterns and learn to manage emotions and behavior.

sources.what_it_said: Treatment for disruptive mood dysregulation disorder generally includes certain types of psychotherapy and sometimes medications. In many cases, psychotherapy is considered first, with medication added later.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy helps the child change negative thoughts into more positive, effective ways of thinking and coping, leading to more effective behavior.

recommended.source_notes: NIMH notes few DMDD-specific treatment studies exist; current treatments are based on what helps related conditions associated with irritability.

recommended.rationale: Parent training in behavior management helps caregivers respond consistently to disruptive and dysregulated behavior, which works well for behavior problems in school-age children as part of a combined approach.

sources.what_it_said: Parent training in behavior management works well for disruptive behavior disorders, and behavior therapy teaches children and their families how to strengthen positive child behaviors and reduce problem behaviors.

recommended.source_notes: Parent training is a core behavioral component across disruptive and dysregulated behavior presentations.

recommended.rationale: Because dysregulation interferes with functioning at school as well as home, treatment may include work with the child's school alongside individual and family therapy.

sources.what_it_said: Treatment may include individual therapy, as well as work with the child's family and/or school.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP explicitly includes the school as part of the treatment plan for chronic irritability and outbursts.

recommended.rationale: DBT adapted for youth teaches skills to better regulate feelings using self-calming techniques, which can reduce the intensity and frequency of emotional outbursts. DBT has the strongest evidence among youth for emotion dysregulation linked to self-harm.

sources.what_it_said: Dialectical behavior therapy for children (DBT-C) teaches children and adolescents how to better regulate their feelings with self-calming techniques, thereby helping to reduce the intensity or frequency of tantrums or outbursts.

A clinical trial of dialectical behavior therapy, which targets emotional control and has been effective in adults, showed that DBT can reduce suicide attempts and suicidal behavior in adolescents who have trouble with emotional control.

recommended.source_notes: Yale Medicine is the university medical center source for DBT-C; NIMH supports DBT for adolescents with emotional control difficulties.

recommended.rationale: CBT helps adolescents identify and change unhelpful thoughts and behaviors and develop healthier ways to express and manage emotions.

sources.what_it_said: Cognitive behavioral therapy helps a person become aware of inaccurate or harmful ways of thinking, question those thoughts, understand how they affect emotions and behavior, and change self-defeating behavior patterns.

recommended.source_notes: General evidence-based psychotherapy applicable to emotion regulation difficulties in adolescents.

recommended.intervention: Medication Management for Specific Symptoms or Co-Occurring Conditions
recommended.rationale: There are no FDA-approved medications specific to chronic irritability; medications may be used to address specific symptoms or co-occurring conditions, typically alongside psychotherapy.

sources.what_it_said: Current treatments are primarily based on what has been helpful for other childhood disorders associated with irritability, and may include psychotherapy and sometimes medications such as stimulants or antidepressants to address specific symptoms.

recommended.source_notes: NIMH cautions that antidepressants may increase suicidal thoughts and behaviors in youth; medication should be monitored by a provider.

recommended.rationale: Persistent sadness, loss of enjoyment, or withdrawal could be due to depression or another condition such as trauma, so a careful evaluation is the first step to determine the right diagnosis and treatment.

sources.what_it_said: Some of the signs and symptoms of depression in children could be caused by other conditions, such as trauma. It is important to get a careful evaluation to get the best diagnosis and treatment.

recommended.source_notes: Depression is less commonly diagnosed in very young children; evaluation is emphasized to rule out other causes.

recommended.rationale: Behavior therapy for young children includes child therapy, family therapy, or a combination, and for very young children involving parents in treatment is key. Play-based approaches help young children express feelings.

sources.what_it_said: Behavior therapy includes child therapy, family therapy, or a combination of both, and the school can also be included; for very young children, involving parents in treatment is key.
Play Therapy uses toys and games to help the child recognize, identify, and verbalize feelings and better understand and manage their feelings and behavior.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP notes evidence for treating depression in pre-pubertal children is notably weaker than for adolescents; approaches here are adapted from general childhood depression and anxiety guidance.

recommended.rationale: Evidence-based therapies to treat depression include cognitive behavioral therapy, which teaches new ways of thinking and behaving and helps change habits that contribute to depression. For milder depression, psychotherapy is often tried first.

sources.what_it_said: Evidence-based therapies to treat depression include cognitive behavioral therapy and interpersonal therapy. For milder forms of depression, psychotherapy is often tried first, with medication added later if therapy alone does not produce a good response.

Cognitive-behavioral therapy is one form of therapy used to treat depression, particularly in older children, helping the child change negative thoughts into more positive, effective ways of thinking and coping.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP notes evidence for psychotherapy is stronger in adolescents than pre-pubertal children, but CBT is the leading approach across school-age depression.

recommended.rationale: Behavior therapy for depression can include child therapy, family therapy, or a combination, with the school included in the treatment plan; engaging caregivers supports the child's recovery.

sources.what_it_said: Engaging parents and other caregivers in treatment is important for children at all ages, and it is important for parents or caregivers to be involved and to provide support to the therapeutic relationship.

recommended.source_notes: CDC emphasizes caregiver involvement as part of treatment for childhood depression.

recommended.rationale: The school can be included in a child's depression treatment plan, providing counseling support and monitoring functioning across settings.

sources.what_it_said: Behavior therapy includes child therapy, family therapy, or a combination of both, and the school can also be included in the treatment plan.

recommended.source_notes: School involvement is named by CDC as part of the depression treatment plan.

recommended.intervention: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Interpersonal Psychotherapy (IPT-A)
recommended.rationale: For depressed adolescents, both CBT and interpersonal psychotherapy are well-established interventions with evidence of efficacy in multiple independent trials. IPT-A helps adolescents handle relationship problems that contribute to depression.

sources.what_it_said: For depressed adolescents, both CBT and interpersonal psychotherapy are well-established interventions, with evidence of efficacy in multiple trials by independent investigative teams. Evidence for pre-pubertal children is notably weaker than for adolescent interventions.
Adolescents with depression may respond well to interpersonal psychotherapy, an approach in which therapists help adolescents learn ways to handle relationship problems.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP identifies CBT and IPT as the two well-established psychotherapies for adolescent depression.

recommended.rationale: A combination of psychotherapy and antidepressant medication appears to be the most effective treatment for adolescents with major depressive disorder, with combined fluoxetine plus CBT also offering increased protection from suicidality.

sources.what_it_said: A combination of psychotherapy and antidepressant medication appears to be the most effective treatment for adolescents with major depressive disorder, more than medication alone or psychotherapy alone, per a major NIMH-funded clinical trial.

There is incremental improvement in outcome when cognitive-behavioral psychotherapy is combined with fluoxetine and, importantly, increased protection from suicidality; CBT should be readily available as part of comprehensive treatment for depressed adolescents.

recommended.source_notes: Based on the NIMH-funded TADS trial summarized by AACAP. Medication requires monitoring for adverse events including suicidality.

recommended.intervention: Suicide Risk Screening and Safety Monitoring
recommended.rationale: Depressed adolescents are at increased risk of self-harm, and the AAP recommends that all youth aged 12 and over be screened for depression and suicide risk during yearly checkups so risk can be identified and managed.

sources.what_it_said: Because adolescents who experience depression are more likely to attempt suicide, the American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that all kids aged 12 and over be screened for depression and suicide risks in yearly health checkups.

Depressed children and adolescents are at higher risk of self-harm, so statements about self-harm should be taken seriously and discussed with the child's pediatrician or a mental health professional.

recommended.source_notes: Screening links depression care to the self_harm_risk pathway. The USPSTF recommends depression screening for adolescents ages 12 to 18 per CDC.

recommended.rationale: TF-CBT is an evidence-based, SAMHSA-recognized treatment for children who have experienced trauma, designed for ages 3 to 18, that builds coping skills and processes the traumatic experience with caregiver involvement.

sources.what_it_said: Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy is a model used with children who have experienced a wide array of types of trauma, and the page reviews relevant research findings and resources for finding certified TF-CBT therapists.
AACAP directs families to trauma resources including the National Child Traumatic Stress Network and SAMHSA's trauma-informed guidance for children exposed to trauma.

recommended.source_notes: TF-CBT is established for ages 3-18; for the youngest children it is delivered with heavy caregiver involvement.

recommended.rationale: Young children may express the effects of trauma through play; play therapy helps them recognize, identify, and verbalize feelings in a safe, accepting relationship.
recommended.rationale_source: AACAP / University of North Texas Center for Play Therapy

sources.what_it_said: Play Therapy uses toys, drawings, and games to help the child recognize, identify, and verbalize feelings, providing an opportunity to better understand and manage conflicts, feelings, and behavior.

sources.organization: University of North Texas Center for Play Therapy
sources.what_it_said: Child-Centered Play Therapy provides a safe, consistent therapeutic environment in which a child can experience full acceptance, empathy, and understanding and process inner experiences and feelings through play.

recommended.source_notes: Play therapy is a recognized modality for young children; for trauma specifically, TF-CBT has the strongest evidence and play-based work supports the youngest age group.

recommended.rationale: Early identification of PTSD is important, and assessment should gather information from both parents and children, especially for young children where caregiver report is essential.

sources.what_it_said: AACAP's practice parameter highlights the importance of early identification of posttraumatic stress disorder and of gathering information from both parents and children, along with assessment of comorbid disorders.

recommended.source_notes: Reflects AACAP PTSD practice parameter guidance; full parameter text is subscription-based on the publisher site.

recommended.rationale: Trauma-focused psychotherapies have the most empirical support for children, and TF-CBT, a family-focused model with strong evidence, improves PTSD, depressive, anxiety, behavioral, and relationship problems.

sources.what_it_said: TF-CBT is a model used with children who have experienced a wide array of types of trauma, and SAMHSA provides reviews of relevant research and resources for finding certified therapists.
AACAP guidance supports trauma-focused psychotherapy, including cognitive-behavioral therapy, for the treatment of children and adolescents with PTSD.

recommended.source_notes: SAMHSA and AACAP both identify trauma-focused CBT as the leading evidence-based treatment for traumatized children.

recommended.rationale: Treatment of children with PTSD should include consultation with school personnel, and school-based screening and treatment are an efficient way to identify and treat affected children after traumatic events.

sources.what_it_said: Treatment of children with PTSD symptoms should include consultation with school personnel, and school-based screening and treatments should be considered after community-level traumatic events as an efficient way to identify and treat affected children.

The Trauma-Informed Services in Schools program increases student access to evidence-based, culturally relevant trauma support services and mental health care by linking local school systems with trauma-informed support and mental health systems.

recommended.source_notes: SAMHSA's TISS program is the federal model for school-based trauma-informed support, directly relevant to a school-based care plan system.

recommended.rationale: Greater parental support and lower parental distress predict more positive outcomes after child trauma, and involving caregivers in treatment effectively improves the child's recovery.

sources.what_it_said: AACAP guidance supports trauma-focused psychotherapy including family therapy, and education of the child and parents, as part of a multimodal approach to childhood PTSD.

recommended.source_notes: Caregiver involvement is a core element of TF-CBT and AACAP's multimodal PTSD approach.

recommended.rationale: TF-CBT is established for youth through age 18 and has the strongest research evidence of any therapy for traumatized youth, teaching skills to manage emotions, build healthy coping, and rebuild a sense of safety.

sources.what_it_said: TF-CBT is used with children and adolescents who have experienced a wide array of types of trauma, and SAMHSA reviews the research and provides resources for finding certified therapists.

recommended.source_notes: TF-CBT applies through adolescence; caregiver involvement remains a recommended component where feasible.

recommended.rationale: Trauma-focused psychotherapies with cognitive-behavioral techniques have the most empirical support for adolescents, including exposure to the traumatic memory, anxiety management, and correcting distorted trauma-related thoughts.

sources.what_it_said: AACAP supports trauma-focused psychotherapy including cognitive-behavioral therapy as having strong support for the treatment of adolescents with posttraumatic stress disorder.

recommended.source_notes: CBT techniques underpin trauma-focused therapy for adolescents.

recommended.rationale: Pharmacotherapy may be considered as part of a multimodal approach to children and adolescents with PTSD, typically alongside trauma-focused psychotherapy rather than as a stand-alone treatment.

sources.what_it_said: AACAP guidance states that pharmacotherapy may be considered in the multimodal approach to children with PTSD, in combination with trauma-focused psychotherapy.

recommended.source_notes: Evidence for SSRIs in pediatric PTSD is limited; medication is an adjunct within a multimodal plan and is the most uncertain recommendation here.

recommended.rationale: For younger children with oppositional and defiant behavior, the treatment with the strongest evidence is behavior therapy training for parents, where a therapist helps the parent strengthen the parent-child relationship and respond effectively to the child's behavior.

sources.what_it_said: For younger children, the treatment with the strongest evidence is behavior therapy training for parents, where a therapist helps the parent learn effective ways to strengthen the parent-child relationship and respond to the child's behavior.

Parent management training in the use of contingency management methods is one of the most substantiated treatment approaches in child mental health, working to reduce reinforcement of disruptive behavior and increase reinforcement of prosocial, compliant behavior.

recommended.source_notes: Strong consensus from CDC and AACAP that parent-focused behavior therapy is first-line for young children with ODD.

recommended.rationale: A behavior disorder may be diagnosed when disruptive behaviors are uncommon for the child's age, persistent, or severe; a comprehensive evaluation helps get the right diagnosis and identify learning or other contributing problems.

sources.what_it_said: The first step to treatment is to talk with a health care provider, and a comprehensive evaluation by a mental health professional may be needed to get the right diagnosis, since some signs could be related to learning problems.

recommended.source_notes: CDC frames evaluation as the first step before treatment for behavior problems.

recommended.rationale: Parent training in behavior management works well for disruptive behavior disorders, including oppositional defiant disorder, and is a core component of effective treatment for school-age children.

sources.what_it_said: Parent training in behavior management works well for disruptive behavior disorders, including oppositional defiant disorder and conduct disorder, and child behavior therapy also works well.
Parent management training is one of the most substantiated treatment approaches in child mental health and is effective in both community and clinical samples.

recommended.source_notes: Parent training remains central for school-age ODD and is combined with child- and school-based components.

recommended.intervention: Combined School Intervention, Individual Therapy, and Parent Training
recommended.rationale: For school-age children and teens, an often-used effective treatment is a combination of training and therapy that includes the child, the family, and the school, ensuring strategies are reinforced across settings.

sources.what_it_said: For school-age children and teens, an often-used effective treatment is a combination of training and therapy that includes the child, the family, and the school.

recommended.source_notes: School-based intervention is explicitly part of the recommended combination for school-age oppositional behavior.

recommended.rationale: One of the two evidence-based treatment types for youth with ODD is an individual approach in the form of problem-solving skills training, which helps the child develop more effective ways of handling conflict and frustration.

sources.what_it_said: The two types of evidence-based treatments for youth with ODD are individual approaches in the form of problem-solving skills training and family interventions.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP identifies problem-solving skills training as an evidence-based individual approach for ODD.

recommended.intervention: Individual Therapy Combined with Parent Training
recommended.rationale: Treatment of ODD should be multimodal, combining individual psychotherapy and parent/family interventions; problem-solving skills training and parent management training are the evidence-based components for older youth.

sources.what_it_said: Treatment of ODD should be multitarget, multimodal, and extensive, combining individual psychotherapy, family psychotherapy, and ecological interventions including school-based interventions, especially when severe and persistent.

recommended.source_notes: AACAP supports a multimodal combination for adolescents with persistent oppositional behavior.

recommended.rationale: Family interventions are one of the two evidence-based treatment types for youth with ODD, and adolescents with disruptive behavior disorders may respond well to family therapy that improves communication and conflict resolution.

sources.what_it_said: The two types of evidence-based treatments for youth with ODD are individual problem-solving skills training and family interventions.

Adolescents with disruptive behavior disorders may respond well to family therapy, an approach that includes multiple members of the family and focuses on learning better communication skills and ways to settle conflicts.

recommended.source_notes: Both AACAP and CDC endorse family-based approaches for adolescent oppositional behavior.

recommended.intervention: Assessment and Treatment of Co-Occurring Conditions
recommended.rationale: Youth with oppositional behavior are predisposed to depression, anxiety, and substance use, so they should be assessed regularly and modifiable risk factors such as bullying addressed.

sources.what_it_said: AACAP guidance emphasizes identifying and treating comorbidities and modifiable risk factors, as youth with oppositional behavior are predisposed to developing depression, anxiety, and substance use.

recommended.source_notes: Comorbidity screening becomes especially important during adolescence.

recommended.intervention: Comprehensive Developmental and Mental Health Evaluation
recommended.rationale: Withdrawal from people and activities can be a sign of an underlying anxiety disorder, depression, trauma, or a developmental condition, so a careful evaluation is needed to identify the cause and the right treatment.

sources.what_it_said: Some of the signs and symptoms of anxiety or depression in children could be caused by other conditions, such as trauma, so it is important to get a careful evaluation to get the best diagnosis and treatment.

recommended.source_notes: Social isolation is a behavioral presentation rather than a diagnosis; evaluation determines whether it reflects anxiety, depression, trauma, or a developmental condition.

recommended.rationale: Play therapy can help socially withdrawn young children experiencing social, emotional, and relational difficulties to process feelings and improve overall functioning within a supportive relationship.
recommended.rationale_source: University of North Texas Center for Play Therapy / AACAP

sources.organization: University of North Texas Center for Play Therapy
sources.what_it_said: Child-Centered Play Therapy is a developmentally responsive intervention for young children ages 3 to 10 experiencing social, emotional, behavioral, and relational disorders, with outcomes including decreased symptomatic behaviors and improved overall functioning.
Play Therapy helps the child recognize, identify, and verbalize feelings and better understand and manage their feelings and behavior.

recommended.source_notes: CCPT explicitly targets social and relational difficulties in young children.

recommended.intervention: School-Based Counseling and Peer Connection Support
recommended.rationale: Difficulty getting along with or socializing with others that interferes with daily life can warrant support; school counseling can monitor functioning and foster peer connection, and the school can be part of the treatment plan.

sources.what_it_said: Strong worries or anxieties that get in the way of daily life, such as at school or socializing, may indicate that a child and adolescent psychiatric evaluation will be useful.
Behavior therapy can include child therapy, family therapy, or a combination of both, and the school can also be included in the treatment plan.

recommended.source_notes: No listed organization provides intervention guidance for social isolation as a standalone condition; recommendations are extrapolated from guidance on social difficulty linked to anxiety and depression.

recommended.intervention: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) for Underlying Anxiety or Depression
recommended.rationale: When withdrawal reflects an underlying anxiety or depressive condition, CBT helps the child change negative thoughts into more effective ways of thinking and coping, supporting re-engagement with peers and activities.

sources.what_it_said: Cognitive-behavioral therapy helps the child change negative thoughts into more positive, effective ways of thinking and coping, leading to more effective behavior.

recommended.source_notes: CBT is indicated when social withdrawal is driven by an identifiable anxiety or depressive condition.

recommended.rationale: Structured social skills support can provide opportunities to practice peer interaction for children whose isolation is linked to social difficulties.

sources.what_it_said: AACAP lists difficulties with socializing and getting along with others as signs that a child and adolescent psychiatric evaluation may be useful.

recommended.source_notes: The social skills training modality has its strongest direct evidence in autism and peer-relationship contexts; its application to general social isolation here is extrapolated, and the cited AACAP source establishes social difficulty as a clinical concern rather than endorsing this specific modality.

recommended.intervention: Evaluation for Depression, Anxiety, and Suicide Risk
recommended.rationale: Social isolation is a recognized risk factor for youth suicide, and withdrawing from activities and isolating from family and friends are warning signs, so evaluation for depression, anxiety, and suicide risk is important.

sources.what_it_said: Social isolation is identified as a risk factor for youth suicide, and behavior changes such as withdrawing from activities and isolating from family and friends are common warning signs.

recommended.source_notes: Links social isolation in adolescents to the self_harm_risk pathway per AAP's youth suicide prevention blueprint.

recommended.rationale: CBT helps adolescents identify and change unhelpful thought patterns that maintain withdrawal and avoidance, supporting re-engagement with peers, school, and activities.

sources.what_it_said: Cognitive behavioral therapy helps a person question inaccurate or harmful thoughts, understand how thoughts affect emotions and behavior, and change self-defeating behavior patterns.

recommended.source_notes: Indicated where withdrawal is driven by an underlying anxiety or depressive condition.

recommended.rationale: Connections to family, friends, and community are protective factors against youth suicide, and school counseling can help re-establish supportive relationships for isolated adolescents.

sources.what_it_said: Protective factors include coping and problem-solving skills, connections to family, friends, and community, and supportive relationships with caregivers.

recommended.source_notes: Fostering connectedness is a protective factor; school is a primary setting for building it.

recommended.rationale: There are no suicide-screening tools validated for children under 8, so when self-harm risk is suspected in a young child a full mental health evaluation is recommended rather than brief screening.

sources.what_it_said: The ASQ is designed to screen patients ages 8 years and above; as there are no tools validated for use in children under the age of 8, if suicide risk is suspected in younger children a full mental health evaluation is recommended instead of screening.

recommended.source_notes: Self-harm risk is rare and atypical at this age; any concern warrants urgent professional evaluation. This knowledge base is not a crisis response tool.

recommended.intervention: Crisis Resources and Caregiver Safety Guidance (988)
recommended.rationale: The 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline provides free, confidential support 24/7 for anyone in crisis or emotional distress, and caregivers should reduce access to potential means of harm in the home.

sources.what_it_said: The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is a national hotline offering one-on-one support for mental health, suicide, and substance use-related problems for anyone 24/7 by call, text, or chat.
Increasing safe storage of lethal means can help reduce suicide attempts and deaths by suicide, and creating a safety or crisis response plan can help reduce a person's risk.

recommended.source_notes: Crisis resources and means restriction apply across all ages; caregiver-led for young children.

recommended.intervention: Suicide Risk Screening and Brief Suicide Safety Assessment
recommended.rationale: Validated screening (the ASQ) identifies youth ages 8 and above who require further assessment, and those who screen positive should receive a brief suicide safety assessment by a trained clinician to determine next steps.

sources.what_it_said: Patients who screen positive for suicide risk on the ASQ should receive a brief suicide safety assessment conducted by a trained clinician to determine if a more comprehensive mental health evaluation is needed; the materials can be used in settings such as the school nursing office.

recommended.source_notes: NIMH ASQ is validated for ages 8 and above and is usable in school settings, directly relevant to a school-based system.

recommended.intervention: Safety Planning and Lethal Means Restriction
recommended.rationale: Creating a safety plan or crisis response plan with specific steps to get help, staying connected and following up, and increasing safe storage of lethal means all help reduce the risk of acting on suicidal thoughts.

sources.what_it_said: Research has shown that creating a safety plan or crisis response plan can help reduce a person's risk of acting on suicidal thoughts, that staying connected and following up helps lower risk, and that increasing safe storage of lethal means can help reduce suicide attempts and deaths.

recommended.source_notes: Safety planning is a clinician-led intervention; means restriction requires caregiver participation.

recommended.intervention: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline and Crisis Services
recommended.rationale: The 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline provides free, confidential, 24/7 support and can connect youth and families to community-based crisis resources, including mobile crisis teams.

sources.what_it_said: Anyone can call or text 988 or chat online 24/7 to connect with a skilled, compassionate crisis counselor; reasons for contacting the Lifeline include emotional distress, anxiety, depression, bullying, and trauma, not only suicide.
If a child, teen, or someone you know needs immediate help, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, which provides free and confidential support 24 hours a day.

recommended.source_notes: Crisis services are a critical safety net across all school-age and adolescent self-harm risk.

recommended.rationale: DBT is the first well-established, empirically supported treatment for decreasing repeated suicide attempts and self-harm in youths, reducing suicide attempts and non-suicidal self-injury in high-risk adolescents.

sources.what_it_said: A clinical trial showed that dialectical behavior therapy can reduce suicide attempts and suicidal behavior in adolescents; by the end of six months, suicide attempts and non-suicidal self-injury were significantly less likely in youth receiving DBT than in those receiving supportive therapy.

sources.organization: University of Washington (McCauley et al., JAMA Psychiatry 2018)
sources.what_it_said: Results support DBT as the first well-established, empirically supported treatment for decreasing repeated suicide attempts and self-harm in highly suicidal, self-harming adolescents.

recommended.source_notes: DBT-A evidence is strongest for adolescents ages 12-18; the advantage over supportive therapy was significant at the end of treatment and narrowed by 6-12 months.

recommended.intervention: Suicide Risk Assessment and Safety Planning
recommended.rationale: Asking directly about suicide does not increase risk and can open the door to help; screening and a safety plan with lethal means restriction reduce the risk of acting on suicidal thoughts.

sources.what_it_said: If you are concerned about your child, ask them directly if they are thinking about suicide; studies show that asking about suicide will not put the idea into their head and could open the door to an honest conversation about their mental health.
Creating a safety plan, staying connected and following up with people at risk, and increasing safe storage of lethal means have all been shown to help reduce suicide risk.

recommended.source_notes: Risk assessment and safety planning should be conducted by trained clinicians; school staff should refer to mental health providers.

recommended.intervention: 988 Crisis Services and Lethal Means Restriction
recommended.rationale: Suicidal thoughts or actions should never be ignored; if a teen is in crisis, contacting 988 connects them with trained staff to determine immediate steps, and lethal means should be removed from the home.

sources.what_it_said: Suicidal thoughts or actions should never be ignored; if a teen is in crisis, call the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline or text TALK to 741741, and trained lifeline staff will help figure out immediate steps to protect the child.
The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline responds 24/7 to calls, chats, or texts and connects those in need with a counselor; mobile crisis teams can support people in their community environments.

recommended.source_notes: Crisis access plus means restriction is a critical adolescent safety component.

recommended.rationale: When self-harm risk is driven by underlying depression, combined CBT plus fluoxetine offers increased protection from suicidality compared with medication alone, though antidepressants require close monitoring.

sources.what_it_said: Combining cognitive-behavioral psychotherapy with fluoxetine provides incremental improvement and, importantly, increased protection from suicidality, with careful monitoring for adverse events recommended.

recommended.source_notes: Medication targets underlying depression; SSRIs carry a monitored risk of increased suicidal thoughts in youth and are used alongside therapy and safety planning.

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: Full text of AOTA Practice Guidelines for Sensory Integration — behind paywall. Only abstracts and table of contents were accessible.

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: SPD is not a standalone diagnosis in DSM-5 — sources do not consistently address SPD as an independent condition. Most AOTA literature frames sensory challenges in the context of ASD or other developmental conditions.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Review ongoing DSM diagnostic discussions and STAR Institute resources on SPD diagnostic validity research

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: Specific evidence-graded recommendations by age group — AOTA and STAR Institute do not differentiate recommendations by specific pediatric age brackets in retrieved sources.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Consult full AOTA Practice Guidelines document for age-specific evidence tables

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: Severity ratings (critical/high/moderate) were assigned based on the emphasis and language used in sources (e.g., 'first line treatment' = critical, 'may be helpful' = moderate) but are not directly sourced classifications.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Verify severity assignments with clinical team review and AAP/AACAP evidence grading systems

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: These seven conditions describe behavioral and emotional presentations reported by guidance counselors, not formal DSM-5 diagnoses. Recommendations were mapped from the closest evidence-based clinical literature for the corresponding disorders, so the fit between an observed presentation and the cited treatment evidence is approximate.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Have a licensed child/adolescent mental health clinician validate the presentation-to-intervention mapping before clinical use

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: School avoidance/refusal is a behavioral presentation addressed in the literature primarily via separation anxiety and the broader anxiety disorders. Age-specific severity ratings were inferred from source emphasis (e.g., AACAP noting adolescent refusal is 'generally a more serious illness').
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Review the full AACAP 2020 Clinical Practice Guideline for Anxiety Disorders (JAACAP) for graded, age-stratified recommendations

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: Emotional dysregulation is not a standalone DSM diagnosis. Recommendations were mapped from disruptive mood dysregulation disorder (DMDD) and irritability literature. NIMH notes few DMDD-specific treatment studies exist, and DBT-C evidence for this presentation is still emerging.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Review NIMH DMDD research updates and emerging DBT-C trials for children with chronic irritability

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: AACAP states evidence for treating depression in pre-pubertal children is notably weaker than for adolescents, so the 3-5 and parts of the 6-12 recommendations are extrapolated from general childhood depression/anxiety guidance rather than age-specific trials. Full text of the AACAP 2022 depression guideline was paywalled.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Access the full AACAP 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline for Major and Persistent Depressive Disorders for age-stratified evidence

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: Full text of the AACAP PTSD Practice Parameter (JAACAP 2010) was behind a paywall; recommendations rely on the abstract and AACAP Disaster Resource Center summaries. Evidence for pharmacotherapy in pediatric PTSD is limited and the medication recommendation is the most uncertain in this condition.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Access the full AACAP PTSD Practice Parameter and current NCTSN treatment reviews for dosage and medication guidance

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: The AACAP ODD Practice Parameter dates to 2007 and notes a limited comparative clinical trial literature. Parent management training effects can wane roughly 12 months after treatment ends, which is not reflected in the static severity ratings.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Review updated PMT/PCIT outcome research and any revised AACAP disruptive behavior guidance for durability of effects

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: Social isolation is not a clinical diagnosis, and none of the approved organizations publish intervention guidance for 'social isolation' as a standalone condition. Recommendations were extrapolated from guidance on social difficulty tied to anxiety/depression and from youth-suicide risk-factor literature. The social skills training modality has its strongest direct evidence in autism and peer-relationship contexts, not general isolation.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Seek peer-reviewed evidence on interventions targeting social withdrawal specifically, and confirm whether isolation is secondary to an underlying diagnosable condition

gaps_and_limitations.what_was_missing: DBT-A evidence is strongest for adolescents ages 12-18; evidence for structured self-harm treatment in children under 12 is limited, and for children under 8 NIMH recommends a full mental health evaluation rather than screening. The McCauley 2018 RCT showed the DBT advantage narrowed by 6-12 months. This knowledge base is not a crisis-response tool.
gaps_and_limitations.suggested_manual_lookup: Establish a clinician-led suicide risk protocol (e.g., NIMH ASQ + Brief Suicide Safety Assessment) and local crisis pathways; do not rely on this file for acute risk decisions
